 Live .  23,653 viewing 23653 viewing Live page Updated 3 minutes ago Flights grounded across US as homeland security secretary says no indication of an attack
 FAA Orders Rare Grounding of All US Flights
 BBC News
 Close Watch live Summary
 Flights have been grounded across the US due to an air traffic control communications issue - here's what we know so far 
 There's no indication that this is an attack against the US, the homeland security secretary says, adding that "everybody's safe" - what else did he say? 
 Markwayne Mullin sought to reassure the public, saying repeatedly that this isn't "another 9/11", our Washington correspondent writes 
 The incident is the largest groundstop in the US since the one after 11 September 2001
 US bound flights from across Europe were suspended after a Federal Aviation Administration request
 Some Asia and Pacific-bound flights were able to depart from certain US airports
 Close form Have you been affected?
 Get in touch Media caption, 'It's going to take some time' - US Homeland Security secretary on nationwide ground stop Live Reporting
 Edited by Christal Hayes and Helen Davidson
 Travellers around the US still stranded at airports published at 01:18 GMT 01:18 GMT 
 As the sun goes down across much of the US, people are still stuck in airports waiting for information on if and when their flights will depart.

 White House about to brief on groundstop published at 00:48 GMT 00:48 GMT 
 We're expecting the US Transport Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to brief reporters shortly.
 When we hear from them, we'll bring you the latest.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Communications outage caused by a network update, CBS reports published at 00:44 GMT 00:44 GMT 
 Multiple sources have told the BBC's US media partner, CBS, that the technical fault behind the nationwide ground stop was caused by an update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system.
 The network, which CBS says is operated by L3Harris, rebooted as a result of the update, and subsequently crashed.
 On its website, L3Harris says it is the "premier provider" of communications systems for the world’s most advanced airspaces, weapon systems and Command and Control platforms.
 L3Harris has not immediately responded to the BBC's request for comment.

 Longest US air traffic grounding event since 9/11, expert says published at 00:35 GMT 00:35 GMT 
 Jake Horton 
BBC Verify 
 Some more comments coming in comparing the current groundstop to previous events.
 During a press conference earlier about the nationwide ground stop, US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin repeatedly said that this "isn't another 9/11".
 BBC Verify has spoken to Dr Guy Gratton, an Associate Professor of Aviation and the Environment at Cranfield University, who agreed and said: "This looks like the worst since 9/11, but clearly not on that scale."
 When asked about comparable incidents, Dr Gratton pointed to a US grounding in 2023 due to a failure in the Notice to Air Missions (Notam) system. 
 "That lasted 1 hour and 52 minutes, delayed about 9,500 flights and cancelled about 1,300," he said.
 The outage meant air traffic safety notices could no longer be published , and flights were grounded until that system was restored.
 That means the current US-wide grounding - which has been in place since 15:54 ET (20:54 GMT) - has now lasted for more than three hours, making it far longer than the 2023 event.

 I'm at Newark but getting out tonight seems unlikely published at 00:29 GMT 00:29 GMT 
 Oliver O'Connell 
 I’m at Newark airport’s Terminal B, where I should be boarding an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles in about an hour. That has now been pushed back by two hours, so getting out tonight seems unlikely.
 Most seating is occupied and small queues have formed at the food and beverage outlets along this concourse. 
 Strangers are having spirited conversations about football to pass the time, while scanning their phones for any updates.
 There was a very short line for security - perhaps an indication that some travellers may have already abandoned their plans.

 'Air traffic controllers are on the job,' says union published at 00:24 GMT 00:24 GMT 
 The National Air Traffic Controllers Association says that as the national ground stop continues to develop, "air traffic controllers are on the job" and "working to ensure the safety of the National Airspace System".
 "The safety of the flying public remains our highest priority,” the union's statement says.

 What we know so far about the US flight groundstop published at 00:05 GMT 00:05 GMT 
 Grace Eliza Goodwin 
US reporter 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images The nationwide ground stop affecting departing flights across the US is still in effect. It's only the second time - and the longest - such a stop has been issued since right after the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks.
 Here's what we know: 
 The stoppage of all flights in the US was ordered a couple hours ago "due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety"
 The problem is related to a telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control centres , US authorities say
 Airports around the country have confirmed the ground stop as some plane passengers report being stuck on the tarmac
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says there's no indication of an attack , all flights are accounted for and " everybody's safe "
 The problem is not connected to the global Microsoft outage that began on Thursday, Mullin says
 American Airlines says it expects the stoppage to last all day while United Airlines says no domestic flights will take off while the ground stop is in place
 Travellers around the country remain stranded as they wait to hear for flight updates 
 We still don't know what specifically caused the issue, how long the stoppage will last, or for how long flights will be delayed or cancelled once the ground stop ends.

 California airport says its cleared for Pacific-bound flights published at 00:01 GMT 00:01 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images We're hearing our first word that some flights are being allowed to take off from San Francisco International airport. 
 The airport posted on social media less than an hour ago that "Pacific-bound flights are now cleared to depart from SFO, including destinations in Hawaii and Asia". 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Biggest ground stop since 9/11, says former NTSB chairman published at 23:53 GMT 13 November 23:53 GMT 13 November 
 The former chairman of the US National Transportation Safety Board says there hasn't been a ground stop of this magnitude in the US since the 11 September attacks in 2001. 
 "This is absolutely unbelievable that this could happen in this day and age," Robert L Sumwalt tells the BBC's US media partner CBS News.
 He mentions that there was a short-lived ground stop in 2023 that only lasted a few hours. 
 Sumwalt says he doesn't yet have a sense of what went wrong but notes that there are 22 air traffic control centres in the United States that are at high altitudes and control airplanes once they are above about 10,000 or 12,000ft ( 3,048 to 3,657m).
 "That's where these outages appear to be happening. It looks like the FAA realises they've got an issue, so they are they're doing the right thing by saying nobody can take off until we get this thing straightened out," he says.
 The FAA has said that the ground stop is due to "reasons of safety",
 "Obviously anytime you have a diminished ability to contact air traffic control, that creates a problem right there," he says. "So again, I think the FAA is doing absolutely the right thing by not ingesting more traffic into a system that is already strained under the current conditions."

 All traffic bound for US suspended, says Eurocontrol published at 23:46 GMT 13 November 23:46 GMT 13 November 
 According to Eurocontrol's website, all US-bound air traffic from Eurocontrol member states has been suspended "on request of the FAA due to technical issues".
 There are 42 Eurocontrol member states, including dozens of EU nations, the UK, Ukraine, and Turkey, as well as two agreement states - Israel and Morocco.
 "For more information check ATCSCC Advisory," the website reads.

 'I'm quite happy to be going home,' says passengers forced to reschedule flight published at 23:36 GMT 13 November 23:36 GMT 13 November 
 Regan Morris 
Reporting from Burbank 
 Gabriel Rivera had just boarded his plane at Burbank Hollywood airport when the captain informed travellers about a "global communications issue".
 Within an hour, he says, they were told the issue could last well into the evening and they were made to deplane and booked on new flights leaving on Saturday.
 The aviation enthusiast says current information suggests airports are currently communicating "manually" with planes due to a radar issue.
 Gabriel adds that despite it all he's "quite happy to be going home" as he would've otherwise have had to "soldier through the delay" into a late night if he hadn't been made to deplane.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Travellers shocked to learn of nationwide grounding published at 23:06 GMT 13 November 23:06 GMT 13 November 
 Regan Morris 
Reporting from Burbank, California 
 Image caption, Taylor and Jack are among those who have been told their flight might not leave on Friday
 Travellers arriving at Burbank Airport expressed relief they made it to ground safely. 
 Others whose flights were not leaving rushed to the rental car line, which is now stretched around the building. 
 Taylor Brothers and Jack Formisani arrived hours early for their flight and were shocked to be told that they might not be flying back to New York today. "It’s nationwide?" Jack asked. 
 The couple just got engaged and were in Los Angeles so Jack could meet Taylor’s family. 
 "That’s so scary," Taylor said when told all flights were grounded. "I don’t think I want to fly today."

 United says no domestic flights will take off while ground stop in place published at 22:53 GMT 13 November 22:53 GMT 13 November 
 United Airlines says new domestic flights will not depart while the ground stop remains in place, but international departures are being managed on a case-by-case basis by the FAA. 
 The airlines has advised passengers to check the latest status of their flights or rebook on their website.

 I'm in the air - and we're still due to land in Cleveland published at 22:50 GMT 13 November 22:50 GMT 13 November 
 Chris Corrall 
Reporting from an Aer Lingus flight 
 I'm currently connected to inflight WiFi on
an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Cleveland, Ohio to see family.
 I found out
about the grounded flights through a message from my wife asking if we were
okay. Shortly after, there was a message from the pilot that all US flights are
grounded. 
 Apparently, some passengers had already seen the news and were
asking if we were going to be impacted.
 Our pilot has since come over the
intercom again to say they've negotiated an earlier landing slot for us, so it
looks like we will still be landing at our destination.

 Flights 'operating normally' north of the border, says Canada air navigation provider published at 22:48 GMT 13 November 22:48 GMT 13 November 
 Nav Canada, which operates the country's civil air navigation system, says that its systems are "operating normally" and the ground stop in the United States is not affecting flights.
 The company adds that it continues to support the safe movement of planes - "including any aircraft that may be diverted".

 American Airlines says disruption expected to last all day published at 22:42 GMT 13 November 22:42 GMT 13 November 
 In a statement, American Airlines says flights already in the air will continue to their destinations, but disruptions to the regular schedule are expected for the remainder of the day.
 “It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible once the FAA lifts this nationwide ground stop,” the airline says.

 What we know about the US flight groundstop published at 22:33 GMT 13 November 22:33 GMT 13 November 
 Image source, Reuters What we know 
 US aviation officials have grounded all flights in the US "due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety"
 The US transportation secretary says that a "communication issue" has hit air traffic control centres and that federal aviation technicians are investigating
 Posting on X, the FAA confirms that a "temporary telecommunications outage" is behind today's rare ground stop, adding that "every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis".
 Flight-tracking website Flightrader24 says that there are 3,100 aircraft in the air and bound for US airports, but no additional aircraft are taking off at this time
 Passengers onboard say that flights that have landed are not allowed to move from the tarmac to the gates
 Several major US airports have confirmed the ground stop, advising passengers to contact their airline before heading to the airport
 The Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that "this isn't another 9/11", seeking to reassure the public 
 Mullin adds that the ground stop is unrelated to the ongoing Microsoft outage
 What we don't know 
 It's unclear how many flights are currently grounded
 It's also unknown what has caused the issue 
 It's unclear how long it will take to resolve the problem
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 US air traffic control is notoriously antiquated published at 22:29 GMT 13 November 22:29 GMT 13 November 
 Theo Leggett 
International business correspondent 
 We don’t know exactly what has caused the current issue,
but US air traffic control systems are notoriously antiquated. 
 Last year,
Congress approved $12.5bn (£9.5bn) for upgrades, but much more is needed.
 Just a couple of weeks ago, the Federal Aviation
Administration pledged to replace systems that still rely on floppy discs - a
form of local data storage that was commonplace in the 1980s and 90s - by the
end of 2028.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Every flight accounted for - FAA published at 22:28 GMT 13 November 22:28 GMT 13 November 
 Posting on X, US aviation officials confirm that a "temporary telecommunications outage" is behind today's rare ground stop. 
 "There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted," the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says. 
 "Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."
